jobs.description:
Bloom is a full-service workplace design consultancy, proudly supporting Poppy & Peonies in their search for a Director of Brand & Social to join their dynamic team. As Talent Advisors, we serve as the bridge between our Bloom Partner and you throughout the recruitment process. At Bloom, we don’t rely on automated tools to sift through applications—every resume is carefully reviewed by a real person to ensure a fair and consistent interview process. If selected, you’ll join Poppy & Peonies directly as a valued member of their team. We’re excited to consider your application! Please note that applications will be accepted throughout the holiday season. Thank you for your patience and interest in this opportunity!

Hi, I’m Natalie Dusome, Founder and CEO of Poppy & Peonies, a fun and energetic brand that believes styles and function should co-exist. We’re passionate about creating practical pieces that help make life a little easier and lighten the load, literally.

Building Poppy & Peonies has been a wild adventure. The journey began when my daughter Poppy was born and my accessories no longer worked with my new life as a mom, I needed bags with pockets and organization that looked cool and had functionality. I couldn’t find it, so I decided to create it, and in 2015 Poppy & Peonies was born.

We’ve come a long way in five years – from filling orders in my basement to appearing on Dragons’ Den, and now, expanding into new product categories and collaborating with some exciting influencers and brands. I’d be lying if I said it’s been nothing but smooth sailing, but thanks to our incredible community, we’ve never felt more loved and supported!

We believe in our responsibility to care for our environment and we are passionate about preserving the health and welfare of our planet, and the animals that live on it. All of our bags are made from high-quality vegan leather, and our entire product line is vegan, cruelty-free, and PETA-approved. We ship our products plastic-free and we use a combination of recycled, compostable, and biodegradable materials to mitigate shipping waste, and we are constantly looking for new ways to make our products and supply chain more sustainable to reduce our carbon footprint.

About the Role

The Director of Planning will lead the integrated Demand Planning, Supply Planning, and Inventory Planning functions at Poppy & Peonies.

This role is responsible for translating commercial plans into actionable inventory and purchasing strategies, ensuring the right products are available in the right quantities, at the right locations, and at the right time.

Working closely with Merchandising, Product Development, Marketing, Finance, Sourcing, and Operations, the Director will establish a disciplined Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) process that balances revenue growth, product availability, inventory productivity, and cash flow.

The ideal candidate combines strong analytical and financial acumen with hands-on planning experience in a fast-paced consumer products environment. They are comfortable working at both strategic and operational levels, building scalable processes while actively managing forecasts, inventory, and purchasing decisions.

The Opportunity

    Demand Planning & Forecasting

  • Own the end-to-end demand forecasting process across all product categories, sales channels, and markets.

  • Develop and maintain rolling demand forecasts at the SKU, category, channel, and distribution center levels.

  • Partner with Merchandising, Marketing, and eCommerce to incorporate product launches, promotional activities, seasonality, marketing investments, and business growth assumptions into forecasts.

  • Lead forecast reviews, analyze actual performance against projections, identify demand trends, and continuously improve forecast accuracy.

  • Develop forecasting methodologies for new product introductions, core replenishment products, and seasonal collections.

  • Identify demand risks and opportunities early and recommend actions to optimize sales and inventory performance.

    • Supply Planning & Purchasing

  • Translate demand forecasts into actionable supply and purchasing plans, considering inventory on hand, open purchase orders, production lead times, transportation lead times, and safety stock requirements.

  • Own the inventory purchasing plan and recommend purchase order quantities, timing, and replenishment strategies.

  • Partner with Global Sourcing and suppliers to align production capacity, lead times, and delivery schedules with business requirements.

  • Support new product launches by ensuring purchase orders and inventory availability align with launch milestones.

  • Proactively identify supply constraints, potential shortages, and excess inventory risks, developing mitigation plans in collaboration with cross-functional teams.

  • Balance product availability with inventory investment and working capital objectives.

    • Inventory Planning & Optimization

  • Develop and execute inventory strategies across multiple distribution centers in Canada and the US.

  • Establish and manage inventory targets, safety stock policies, and SKU classifications based on demand patterns, product lifecycle, and business priorities.

  • Monitor weeks of supply (WOS), inventory turns, stock availability, and aging inventory.

  • Recommend inventory allocation and replenishment strategies across markets and distribution centers.

  • Identify slow-moving and excess inventory and work with Merchandising and Marketing on appropriate actions.

  • Optimize inventory positioning to improve service levels while minimizing carrying costs, transfers, and markdown exposure.

    • Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP)

  • Design, implement, and lead a structured monthly S&OP process, integrating commercial demand, supply capabilities, inventory investment, and financial objectives.

  • Facilitate cross-functional planning discussions and drive alignment on a single, consensus-based operating plan.

  • Partner with Finance to reconcile sales forecasts, inventory purchases, open-to-buy (OTB) plans, and financial targets.

  • Provide leadership with clear visibility into demand and supply risks, inventory requirements, and key business trade-offs.

  • Develop scenario planning capabilities to support business decisions related to growth, promotions, product launches, and supply disruptions.

  • Establish clear planning cadences, accountability, and decision-making processes.

    • Product Launch & Lifecycle Planning

  • Partner with Product Development, Merchandising, and Sourcing to support seasonal assortment planning and new product introductions.

  • Develop initial demand forecasts and inventory buy recommendations for new collections based on historical performance, comparable products, and commercial assumptions.

  • Align purchasing decisions with product development milestones, supplier lead times, and launch dates.

  • Monitor launch performance and recommend inventory reallocation, replenishment, or exit strategies.

  • Manage inventory planning throughout the product lifecycle, including introduction, growth, replenishment, and end-of-life.

    • Planning Systems, Analytics & Process Improvement

jobs.companyName: World University Service of Canada (WUSC - EUMC)
jobs.description:
Terms of Reference (ToR): Rapid Assessment of the Context of and Opportunities for Refugees and Displaced Youth in Nigeria.

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Interested applicants are encouraged to submit their applications early.

  1. Background

Nigeria hosts substantial populations of Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), refugees and asylum seekers, with displacement driven by armed conflict, insecurity, intercommunal tensions and climate-related pressures. As of 1 October 2026, available figures indicate approximately 3.7 million IDPs and 141,688 refugees and asylum seekers.

Displaced youth aged 18–35 face multiple barriers to education, skills development, employment, entrepreneurship and economic participation. These include disrupted educational pathways, limited access to training and financial services, documentation requirements, restricted economic opportunities, and social exclusion. Young women and youth with disabilities may experience additional barriers. These barriers may be compounded by intersecting factors such as age, gender, disability, displacement status, socioeconomic circumstances and geographic location. Gender norms, unpaid care responsibilities, safety concerns and limited accessibility may further constrain participation in education and economic opportunities. However, the circumstances of refugees, asylum seekers and IDPs differ considerably, including in terms of their legal status, access to services, institutional support and opportunities for economic inclusion.

These differences are also shaped by geography, local economic conditions, government policies and the capacities and incentives of institutions responsible for supporting displaced populations.

The Mastercard Foundation, through its partnership with WUSC under the DREEM project, seeks to strengthen opportunities for refugees and displaced youth (RDPs) to access education, develop relevant skills and participate meaningfully in economic life. In Nigeria, there is particular interest in understanding opportunities to strengthen the inclusion of internally displaced youth, alongside refugees and asylum seekers.

A rapid contextual assessment is therefore proposed to consolidate existing evidence, examine the institutional and structural factors shaping RDP inclusion, and identify practical opportunities for future programming, partnerships and policy engagement.

2. Purpose of the Assessment

The assessment aims to generate practical, context-specific evidence on the barriers and
opportunities affecting the inclusion of refugees and internally displaced youth in Nigeria,

particularly in education, skills development, employment, entrepreneurship and broader economic participation.It will examine the policy, institutional, socioeconomic and political economy factors shaping these opportunities, including the roles and incentives of relevant government institutions, private sector actors, development partners and refugee- and IDP-led organizations. The assessment will apply an intersectional lens to understand how barriers and opportunities differ among displaced youth, particularly young women, youth with disabilities and those experiencing multiple forms of exclusion.

The assessment will inform the Mastercard Foundation's and DREEM's understanding of th Nigerian context and help identify feasible areas for programmatic support, institutional

partnerships and policy engagement.

At Clover, the Business Enablement team leads our technological advancement while ensuring robust security and compliance. We deliver user-friendly corporate applications, manage complex data ecosystems, and provide efficient tech solutions across the organization. Our goal is simple: we make it easy for the business to do what’s right for Clover.

We’re hiring a Director of Product to build and lead a product function in Clover's new R&D function. Reporting directly to the CTO, the scope of you and your team will span health-plan, care services, and corporate technology.

This is a player-coach role. You will personally work through difficult product questions while developing a small, flat team of product managers and embedded product operations staff. Most PM assignments will pursue one or two defined outcomes through repeated research and experiments. A small number of senior assignments will require judgment across ambiguous problem spaces to identify and shape the next project worth doing.

You will lead product craft across R&D from the outset, while drawing on the product expertise of Counterpart, our separate technology subsidiary. The surface area is large, and Product missions and capacity will evolve with the business needs and evidence.

You’ll work with empowered teams and individuals: our engineers work directly with users, exercise product judgment, and own technical execution. Many operational needs are clear and practical technical solutions are available; the harder work is resolving details, ownership, and adoption. Our bias is to build the simplest useful system and iterate quickly. You will recognize when engineers and operating owners can advance directly, where a PM can improve a defined outcome, and where substantial product or design discovery is needed.

As a Director of Product, you will:

  • Build and develop the product team. Hire for the work, give direct feedback, coach research and measurement, and grow people’s judgment while keeping the structure proportionate to the team.
  • Build a culture within product and engineering that values incremental progress toward measurable outcomes, clear stakeholder communication, and aggressive AI-forward productivity.
  • Understand the member journey across plan and clinical operations. Observe the work, review interactions and data, and connect apparent technology problems to the underlying needs of members and staff.
  • Choose focused product missions with business and engineering partners. Decide where dedicated product attention will help and match the assignment to the uncertainty: a defined improvement mission or senior discovery across a broader problem space. Establish useful baselines, define success, test assumptions, and change course when the evidence warrants it.
  • Personally investigate ambiguous opportunities. Turn them into a clear problem, evidence of value, a plausible approach, and a useful first delivery or learning milestone.
  • Develop an embedded Product Operations function that connects frontline observation, testing, training, and adoption to product and engineering decisions.
  • Partner closely with product leaders in other organizations, Special Project Leads, clinical leaders, and operating owners. Make ownership clear across shared journeys and capabilities.
  • Use AI directly to investigate ideas, build and test prototypes, and run bounded experiments. Check the outputs and use what you learn to choose the next step. Work with engineering and operating owners to take promising experiments into production; engineering retains technical delivery and readiness, and operating owners accept the resulting workflow.

Success in this role looks like:

  • First 90 days: You understand the initial member and operational journeys, have selected focused product missions with engineering and operating partners, and can explain where teams can advance directly. You are personally advancing a difficult product question, coaching the initial PM work, and establishing credible evidence from an improvement or experiment.
  • First six months: PMs exercise stronger judgment and independently advance their assigned missions. Senior discovery produces focused projects and well-supported decisions to defer or stop. Shipped changes are being used, and product decisions connect to measurable improvements in member experience, operational effectiveness, or unit economics.

You should get in touch if:

  • You have led and developed product managers while remaining personally involved in discovery, prioritization, and difficult product decisions.
  • You have built or substantially shaped a product function and are comfortable starting with a small team and an evolving remit.
  • You have improved products used in real operational workflows and can connect software, human work, business economics, and adoption.
  • You use AI heavily in your own work and have a practical view of its capabilities and limitations, and strong hypotheses about its future.
  • You are technically fluent in systems, APIs, data, and AI behavior. You can independently investigate an idea, build and test a prototype, and run a bounded experiment using AI. You can understand the architectural implications of the products you help design.
  • You use research, data, and experiments to make decisions, and can distinguish a promising observation from evidence strong enough to act on.
  • You work effectively with engineers who exercise broad judgment and with operating leaders who own their businesses. You build trust through direct relationships and clear decisions.

Benefits Overview:

  • Financial Well-Being: Our commitment to attracting and retaining top talent begins with a competitive base salary and equity opportunities. Additionally, we offer a performance-based bonus program, 401k matching, and regular compensation reviews to recognize and reward exceptional contributions.
  • Physical Well-Being: We prioritize the health and well-being of our employees and their families by providing comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage. Your health matters to us, and we invest in ensuring you have access to quality healthcare.
  • Mental Well-Being: We understand the importance of mental health in fostering productivity and maintaining work-life balance. To support this, we offer initiatives such as No-Meeting Fridays, monthly company holidays, access to mental health resources, and a generous flexible time-off policy. Additionally, we embrace a remote-first culture that supports collaboration and flexibility, allowing our team members to thrive from any location.
  • Professional Development: Developing internal talent is a priority for Clover. We offer learning programs, mentorship, professional development funding, and regular performance feedback and reviews.

Additional Perks:

  • Reimbursement for office setup expenses
  • Monthly cell phone & internet stipend
  • Remote-first culture, enabling collaboration with global teams
  • Paid parental leave for all new parents
  • And much more!

About Clover: We are reinventing health insurance by combining the power of data with human empathy to keep our members healthier. We believe the healthcare system is broken, so we've created custom software and analytics to empower our clinical staff to intervene and provide personalized care to the people who need it most.

We always put our members first, and our success as a team is measured by the quality of life of the people we serve. Those who work at Clover are passionate and mission-driven individuals with diverse areas of expertise, working together to solve the most complicated problem in the world: healthcare.

From Clover’s inception, Diversity & Inclusion have always been key to our success. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and our employees are people with different strengths, experiences, perspectives, opinions, and backgrounds, who share a passion for improving people's lives. Diversity not only includes race and gender identity, but also age, disability status, veteran status, sexual orientation, religion and many other parts of one’s identity. All of our employee’s points of view are key to our success, and inclusion is everyone's responsibility.

jobs.excerpt: About DonorboxDonorbox is a leading fundraising platform and donor management system for nonprofit organizations.
jobs.description:
About Donorbox

Donorbox is a leading fundraising platform and donor management system for nonprofit organizations. Our mission is to accelerate positive impact worldwide by helping nonprofits become highly effective at raising funds and managing their supporter base. Since 2014, we have powered more than 100,000 global organizations to raise over $4 billion in donations. 🚀

Our fast-growing company is profitable and bootstrapped with a healthy run rate. We have a fully distributed and diverse 150-person team based in 16+ states and 23+ countries. In 2026, Donorbox was named by Built In as one of the Best Places to Work in Washington, DC.

🏅 Donorbox is rated the #1 software for fundraising, donor management, and nonprofit payment on G2 based on hundreds of verified customer reviews — a reflection of the care our team puts into building products that nonprofits trust.

The Role

As Corporate Counsel, you’ll be Donorbox's in-house lawyer. You’ll own our day-to-day legal work, manage our outside counsel on specialized matters, and act as the legal partner to every team in the company: Sales, Partnerships, Product and Engineering, Customer Success, Finance and People. You’ll also manage our Senior Compliance Manager, setting priorities and partnering closely on regulatory, privacy and security compliance.

This is not a back-office or narrow specialist role. We are looking for a business partner who happens to be a lawyer: someone who uses legal as an advantage for the company, not only as a defense. You won't hand the business a bare "yes" or "no." You'll bring options, the risk level of each, and a recommendation, and you'll be comfortable standing behind that recommendation.

What You'll Own

1. Commercial Contracts & Revenue Enablement

  • Draft, review and negotiate complex enterprise and SaaS customer agreements, balancing risk with the commercial reality of winning and expanding business.
  • Set clear guardrails for pricing, discounts, custom terms and non-standard agreements, with defined fallbacks and approval thresholds.
  • Build a contract playbook and standard templates so most deals close without bespoke legal review.
  • Work with Finance to build the right financial mechanics into contracts (payment terms, multi-year commitments, renewals, termination rights) so they match how we model revenue.
  • Design collections and recovery terms, including clawback provisions.
  • Support customer procurement, privacy and security reviews, and partner with Sales and Customer Success to remove legal friction from closing and retaining customers.

2. Partnerships, Channel & Vendor Agreements

  • Create the frameworks, standards and templates that let our partnerships scale: technology and integration partners, payment providers, hardware and fulfillment vendors, denominational and network partners, and referral, ambassador and reseller programs.
  • Structure revenue share, exclusivity, liability allocation, data ownership, termination rights and joint branding.
  • Balance legal protection with commercially workable terms that preserve partner relationships.
  • Negotiate vendor agreements that protect Donorbox when we don't get what we pay for.
  • Resolve live contractual issues with technology, hardware and payment partners.

3. Product, Regulatory, Privacy & AI

  • Monitor the rules that govern our business: online fundraising, payments, platform fees and tipping, PCI, nonprofit regulation, and the growing set of state laws that regulate donation platforms directly.
  • Reason from first principles about what the law actually requires, separate real obligations from industry noise, and weigh the cost of compliance work against the risk it removes.
  • Own privacy compliance across GDPR, CCPA and state privacy laws.
  • Guide the responsible use of AI and customer data. You'll learn how our systems work under the hood, so your guidance protects private data without blocking the product.
  • Partner with Engineering on security governance, including SOC 2, audits and customer security requirements.
  • Lead regulatory work as we expand into new markets, and spot where the regulatory landscape creates an opening for Donorbox, not only a risk.
  • Divide legal and compliance work with the Senior Compliance Manager, so routine compliance runs without your direct involvement and escalations reach you quickly.

4. Customer Escalations & Disputes

  • Advise Customer Success on complex customer issues, including account suspension and termination decisions.
  • Set clear escalation paths for disputes, fraud, regulatory inquiries and threatened or active litigation.
  • Provide approved language for high-risk incidents, investigations and sensitive customer communications.
  • Manage litigation and disputes with outside counsel.

5. Employment & Corporate Risk

  • Draft and maintain offer letters, employment agreements and contractor agreements, and manage worker classification.
  • Give managers the confidence and process to address performance and conduct issues promptly, with clear documentation and one high standard applied consistently to everyone.
  • Advise on separations and lead legally sensitive employee investigations, bringing in outside counsel where the matter calls for it.
  • Partner with People on employment policies, and advise on international employment as we hire outside the U.S.
  • Own the company's insurance program, including D&O, E&O, cyber and general liability.

6. Corporate, Equity & IP

  • Own equity administration and the cap table (Carta) in partnership with Finance.
  • Support corporate governance and Board matters, and serve as a trusted legal advisor to the CEO and executive team.
  • Prepare the company for future financings and take on corporate work in-house where it makes sense, reducing reliance on outside counsel.
  • Manage our trademark portfolio, enforce our brand, and respond to competitor misrepresentation.
  • Protect our IP across product, technology, content and brand, with sound IP assignment from employees, contractors and partners.

Your First 90 Days

  • Map the landscape. Assess active matters, contracts, policies, outside counsel and compliance obligations, and deliver a prioritized legal roadmap.
  • Right-size outside counsel. Set a clear framework for when we use outside counsel and when we handle work in-house.
  • Close regulatory gaps. Assess Donorbox against the state donation-platform and fundraising laws that apply to us, and recommend fixes.
  • Unblock the business. Resolve the highest-priority partner, vendor and customer agreements that are slowing us down today.
  • Launch the playbooks. Ship the first commercial contract playbook and partnership templates, with standard positions, fallbacks and approval thresholds.
  • Set the operating rhythm. Make "options, risk levels, recommendation" the default for legal advice, with clear escalation paths for every team.

What We're Looking For

  • A U.S. law degree (J.D.) and active bar admission in at least one U.S. state.
  • 5+ years of legal experience, including at least 4 years in-house at a SaaS or high-growth technology company.
  • Experience as the sole or most senior lawyer at a company, or the #2 lawyer on a legal team of five or fewer.
  • Hands-on experience negotiating enterprise SaaS and partnership agreements.
  • Hands-on experience with employment matters, including terminations, investigations and employment agreements.
  • Working knowledge of privacy and compliance frameworks such as GDPR, CCPA and PCI.
  • Experience managing outside law firms and an outside counsel budget.
  • Curiosity about technology: you pick up technical concepts quickly, get the nuances right, and understand how AI and data systems work well enough to advise on them with confidence.
  • Sound business judgment, comfort making calls under ambiguity, and the ability to explain legal issues plainly to executives and non-lawyers.
  • Experience managing or mentoring another legal or compliance professional (preferred).

Especially Valuable

  • Payments or fintech
  • Nonprofit technology, online fundraising or faith-based organizations
  • Marketplace or platform regulation
  • Hardware or physical-product supply chains
  • International expansion
  • Equity administration, financings, or M&A

You'll Thrive Here If You

  • Think like a business operator, not only a lawyer.
  • Can tell a theoretical legal risk from a material business risk, and know when to accept risk to move faster and when to hold the line.
  • Would rather build a scalable playbook than review the same issue twice.
  • Know when to call outside counsel and when to make the call yourself.
  • Move quickly without getting careless.
  • Write in plain English. Your advice is short, clear and easy to act on.
  • Are comfortable saying, "Here are three ways we can do this, here is the risk of each, and here is what I recommend."

Details

  • Fully remote based in the United States. Washington, D.C. area preferred. Must work Eastern Time business hours (Central Time also considered).
  • Salary: $190,000–$220,000, based on experience, skills and location

Benefits & Perks

  • Fully remote work from the comfort of your home
  • Generous time off policy of 21 days (birthday included 🎉), 8 designated/floating holidays, 2 paid volunteer days, and 5 sick days
  • Employer-sponsored health insurance plan through TriNet, including medical (United Healthcare), dental, vision, and life
  • 401(k) retirement plan via TriNet's partner, Empower, with an employer match of up to 4%
  • Reimbursement package for home office expenses and professional development, up to $1.5k
  • Eligibility for employee equity plan (stock options)
  • Wellness program with fitness and mindfulness classes
  • Love your work and our mission of serving nonprofits!

The Application Process

About Plan A

Plan A, a Diginex Ltd company, is Europe’s leading corporate carbon accounting and decarbonisation software provider, helping companies turn emissions intelligence into financial performance. Its AI-powered, TÜV-certified platform, coupled with expert support, simplifies emissions accounting, target setting, and reduction planning in line with GHG, and SBTi standards.

We are looking for a hands-on and proactive Finance & Accounting Specialist to strengthen our European Finance team.

About the Role

In this role, you will take ownership of day-to-day accounting activities, support monthly closing and reporting, and help streamline accounting processes across our European entities.

You will work closely with the Finance Director, internal stakeholders and external accounting partners, with a particular focus on our German operations and the gradual integration of accounting activities in France.

This position is ideal for someone who enjoys operational accounting, takes responsibility and wants to contribute to improving processes in an international environment.

Your Responsibilities

General Accounting & Month-End Closing

  • Manage day-to-day bookkeeping and general ledger accounting, primarily using DATEV.
  • Process and reconcile accounts payable and accounts receivable.
  • Review supplier invoices, employee expenses and payment transactions.
  • Perform bank, credit card and balance sheet reconciliations.
  • Prepare and support monthly closing activities, including accruals, prepayments and accounting adjustments.
  • Maintain accurate accounting records and supporting documentation.

European Accounting & Coordination

  • Support accounting activities across our European entities, particularly Germany and France.
  • Gradually take over selected operational bookkeeping tasks currently performed by external accounting providers.
  • Support intercompany accounting, reconciliations and transaction documentation.
  • Coordinate with external accountants and local service providers.
  • Assist with accounting-related questions and the preparation of information for group reporting.

Financial Operations & Process Improvement

  • Support billing reconciliations and ensure consistency between customer contracts, invoicing and accounting records.
  • Assist with payment preparation and supplier account reconciliations.
  • Identify discrepancies and follow up on outstanding accounting items.
  • Improve and standardise accounting workflows, reconciliations and internal controls.
  • Support audit preparation and documentation requirements.

Requirements

What we're looking for

  • Several years of practical experience in financial accounting, bookkeeping or a comparable role.
  • Solid knowledge of German accounting principles (HGB) and general ledger processes.
  • Good hands-on experience with DATEV.
  • Experience in accounts payable, accounts receivable, bank reconciliations and monthly closing.
  • Comfortable working with Excel and accounting data.
  • Good German and English communication skills.
  • Independent, structured and detail-oriented working style.
  • A proactive and pragmatic approach to solving problems.

What makes you stand out

  • Experience working in an international or multi-entity organisation.
  • Familiarity with accounting processes in France or other European countries.
  • Experience with Payhawk, Pennylane or comparable financial systems.
  • Experience improving or internalising accounting processes previously handled by external providers.
  • Exposure to SaaS businesses or recurring-revenue models.

What matters to us

We value practical experience, reliability and a willingness to take ownership over formal titles or conventional career paths.

We welcome applications from professionals with different backgrounds, including those returning to work after a career break.

You do not need to have worked in an international group before. What matters most is that you understand accounting, enjoy working hands-on and are motivated to learn.

Benefits

What you can expect from Plan A

  • A permanent position within an international Finance organisation.
  • The opportunity to take ownership of operational accounting processes.
  • Direct collaboration with the Finance Director.
  • Exposure to accounting activities across several European entities.
  • The possibility to work fully remotely from anywhere in Germany.
  • The opportunity to improve processes and help shape a more efficient Finance function.

Each day, our employees do the can’t be done by solving the most daunting challenges facing our customers. Visit peraton.com to learn how we’re keeping people around the world safe and secure.

Responsibilities

Peraton is seeking an experienced Core Services Mobility Lead to oversee the architecture, engineering, operations, and support of enterprise mobility services. This individual will provide technical leadership for the mobility environment, with a primary focus on BlackBerry Unified Endpoint Management (UEM), Apple device management, Microsoft Intune integration, identity services, and mobile security.

The Core Services Mobility Lead will serve as the technical authority for mobility architecture and engineering decisions, ensuring solutions align with enterprise requirements, security standards, and operational objectives. The ideal candidate will bring extensive experience in enterprise mobility management, Microsoft technologies, mobile device security, and technical team leadership.

Location: This position is fully remote.

Day to Day Responsibilities

Technical Leadership and Architecture

  • Own the enterprise mobility architecture and approve technical changes involving identity management, Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), Microsoft 365, and Apple technologies.

  • Lead, mentor, and provide technical direction to the Core Services engineering team.

  • Establish engineering standards and best practices while promoting collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement.

  • Serve as the primary technical representative for mobility services across TSA, Peraton, and external vendors.

  • Provide technical guidance and serve as the final escalation point for complex Unified Endpoint Management (UEM) issues.

Mobility Engineering and Operations

  • Lead the design, implementation, upgrades, and ongoing support of BlackBerry UEM and BlackBerry Enterprise Mobility Server (BEMS).

  • Maintain existing zero-touch iOS enrollment capabilities using Apple Business Manager (ABM), Automated Device Enrollment (ADE), and Apple Push Notification service (APNs) certificates.

  • Coordinate with End User Services (EUS) to support required Apple enrollment and certificate updates.

  • Maintain the Microsoft Intune integration, including App Protection Policies and Compliance Partner integration with UEM through Microsoft Graph. Intune supports application protection and compliance integration and is not the primary Mobile Device Management (MDM) platform.

  • Design and maintain certificate delivery solutions for mobile devices using Simple Certificate Enrollment Protocol (SCEP) and Public Key Cryptography Standards (PKCS).

  • Identify opportunities to improve mobility services, infrastructure performance, operational efficiency, and service delivery.

Security and Compliance

  • Map Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) mobile Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs) to applicable mobility policies and configurations.

  • Review each new iOS release to assess security implications, compatibility, and required policy updates.

  • Ensure mobility engineering solutions align with established security requirements, enterprise policies, and applicable compliance standards.

  • Identify, assess, and mitigate technical and operational risks affecting the mobility environment.

Infrastructure Operations and Service Delivery

  • Support the operations, maintenance, and engineering of enterprise IT infrastructure, including Microsoft Windows Server environments.

  • Ensure engineering activities align with established change, release, and configuration management processes.

  • Monitor ongoing work, resolve technical issues, and communicate operational status and risks to management.

  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams and stakeholders to coordinate infrastructure and mobility activities.

Qualifications

About Extend:

Extend is revolutionizing the post-purchase experience for retailers and their customers by providing merchants with AI-driven solutions that enhance customer satisfaction and drive revenue growth. Our comprehensive platform offers automated customer service handling, seamless returns/exchange management, end-to-end automated fulfillment, and product protection and shipping protection alongside Extend's best-in-class fraud detection. By integrating leading-edge technology with exceptional customer service, Extend empowers businesses to build trust and loyalty among consumers while reducing costs and increasing profits.

Today, Extend works with more than 1,000 leading merchant partners across industries, including fashion/apparel, cosmetics, furniture, jewelry, consumer electronics, auto parts, sports and fitness, and much more. Extend is backed by some of the most prominent technology investors in the industry, and our headquarters is in downtown San Francisco.

About the Role:

As a Claims Adjudication Specialist, you will play a critical role within our Operations Department, focused on evaluating and servicing claims related to our Product and Shipping Protection plans, which are offered by over 1,000+ Merchant Partners. You’ll serve as a subject matter expert, supporting our Customer Support and Service Technician partners to ensure accurate and timely service of complex claims that require deeper investigation.

This position requires strong analytical skills, critical thinking, and the ability to interpret multiple policies across a wide range of product categories. On a daily basis, you’ll review complex claim submissions, manage escalations, and investigate unusual claim patterns. Success in this role relies on meticulous attention to detail, evidence-based decision-making and ability to adapt to frequent change in processes and technology within a fast-paced environment.

You'll collaborate closely with customers, service partners, and internal teams to deliver accurate claim decisions while ensuring an exceptional customer experience. The role involves inbound and outbound calls, as well as written communications with customers, service providers, and internal stakeholders.

Responsibilities:

  • Serves as the escalation point of contact from outsourced partners, customer support teams and service technician partners.
  • Investigate and resolve complex claim situations, ensuring decisions align with contract terms and internal policies.
  • Troubleshoot delays in claims processing, ensuring timely resolutions and enhanced customer satisfaction.
  • Coordinate service technician dispatching and parts ordering when necessary to support claim resolution.
  • Resolve escalated customer issues by proposing fair resolutions within policy guidelines and clearly communicating outcomes to the customer.
  • Maintain detailed and organized documentation of all customer and partner interactions.
  • Investigate suspected fraudulent claims and report findings as needed.
  • Recommend process improvements and opportunities to automate routine tasks.
  • Provide timely responses to claim inquiries via phone and email, in line with established SLAs.
  • Collaborate with Product and Engineering teams to troubleshoot and escalate unresolved claim issues.
  • Stay up to date on product offerings, service workflows, and policy updates to better support customers.
  • Identify and communicate training needs for front-line support teams to improve service quality.
  • Keep internal systems current with relevant technical issues, customer feedback, and insights.

Preferred Experience, Skills, and Knowledge:

  • Active adjuster licenses (preferred).
  • 3-5 years of technical customer service, claims management/adjudication, insurance adjusting, or contact center experience. Claims adjudication preferably in a protection plan environment.
  • Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written with the ability to convey complex claim details and supporting rationale for decisioning in a clear and concise way both to customers and internal system notations.
  • Embraces frequent change in processes and technology within a fast-paced environment, demonstrating flexibility and resilience in managing evolving challenges.
  • Experienced with claims management systems, contact center platforms, and Google suites of products.
  • Proven ability to to navigate and work effectively across various software systems simultaneously.
  • Ability to analyze complex issues, identify solutions, and make decisions efficiently.
  • Thrive in environments of high claim volumes with exponential company growth while maintaining excellent performance and accuracy.

Estimated Pay Range: $45,000 - $55,000 per year salaried*

*The target base salary range for this position is listed above. Individual salaries are determined based on a number of factors including, but not limited to, work location and job-related knowledge, skills and experience.

Extend does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role.

Life at Extend:

  • Working with a great team from diverse backgrounds in a collaborative and supportive environment.
  • Competitive salary based on experience, with full medical and dental & vision benefits.
  • Stock in an early-stage startup growing quickly.
  • Generous, flexible paid time off policy.

About the team

The Workforce Planning team sits at the center of Zillow’s customer-facing operations, helping ensure we have the right plans, tools, and insights in place to deliver a seamless experience for customers and sellers. We partner closely with leaders across operations, sales, finance, and technology to shape forecasting, capacity planning, scheduling, and real-time performance strategies that support both business outcomes and a strong colleague experience. The team is organized into Command Center, Resource Planning, and Capacity Planning, each led by a dedicated leader. This team plays a key role in building scalable, data-informed frameworks that help Zillow grow thoughtfully while keeping our customers and employees at the heart of every decision.

About the role

The Director, Workforce Planning leads the strategy, planning, and execution of enterprise workforce management for Zillow’s customer-facing operations, ensuring the right people are in the right place at the right time to deliver an exceptional experience. This leader of leaders sets the vision for long-range capacity planning, forecasting, scheduling, and real-time performance management across contact center environments, using data-driven insights to optimize service levels, productivity, and colleague experience. The Director collaborates closely with senior business, operations, finance, and technology leaders to design scalable frameworks, challenge the status quo, and enable sustainable growth.


  • Set the enterprise workforce management strategy for contact center operations, aligning capacity planning, staffing, and service level targets with Zillow’s business objectives and customer experience goals.
  • Lead long-range and annual workforce planning, including demand forecasting, hiring plans, and budget inputs across sites, lines of business, and channels to support growth while managing cost and risk.
  • Design and govern standardized WFM policies, frameworks, and KPIs (e.g., forecast accuracy, schedule adherence, occupancy, service levels) to ensure consistent practices and performance visibility across teams.
  • Oversee the workforce management operating model and teams, including forecasting, scheduling, and real-time management functions, providing leadership, coaching, and development to team leaders and analysts.
  • Partner with Operations, Sales, Finance, HR, and vendor partners to align staffing strategies with volume trends, productivity goals, and workforce initiatives, enabling data-informed decisions on hiring, training, and deployment.
  • Champion the roadmap for WFM tools and technology, including AI, collaborating with Product, Engineering, and vendor partners to implement and optimize workforce management systems, telephony routing, and reporting solutions.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives that enhance forecast accuracy, schedule efficiency, shrinkage management, and intraday execution, using analytics and experimentation to test and scale best practices.
  • Provide executive-level insights and recommendations through clear storytelling, dashboards, and operational reviews, highlighting risks, opportunities, and trade-offs in staffing and performance.
This role has been categorized as a Remote position. “Remote” employees do not have a permanent corporate office workplace and, instead, work from a physical location of their choice, which must be identified to the Company. U.S. employees may live in any of the 50 United States, with limited exceptions.In California, Connecticut, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Jersey, New York, Washington state, and Washington DC the standard base pay range for this role is $142,500.00 - $227,600.00 annually. The base pay range is specific to these locations and may not be applicable to other locations.In addition to a competitive base salary this position is also eligible for equity awards based on factors such as experience, performance and location. Actual amounts will vary depending on experience, performance and location. Employees in this role will not be paid below the salary threshold for exempt employees in the state where they reside.

Who you are

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Operations Management, Mathematics, Statistics, Finance, Industrial Engineering, or a related field.
  • 10+ years of experience in workforce management, contact center operations, or a closely related field, including 5+ years in a people leadership role leading multi-function teams.
  • Demonstrated experience owning enterprise or large-scale workforce planning, forecasting, and scheduling for high-volume, multi-channel environments (e.g., service or support), including BPO vendor partners.
  • Proven success using data and analytics to diagnose performance drivers, improve forecast accuracy, and optimize staffing, productivity, and customer or sales outcomes.
  • Track record of influencing senior leaders and cross-functional partners with clear, data-driven recommendations in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.
  • Working knowledge of WFM platforms such as Aspect, Genesys, or NICE, and related telephony or CRM tools.

Get to know us

At Zillow, we’re reimagining how people move—through the real estate market and through their careers. As the most-visited real estate platform in the U.S., we help people navigate buying, selling, financing and renting with greater ease and confidence. Whether you're working in tech, sales, operations, or design, you’ll be part of a company reshaping an industry and helping more people make home a reality.


How we work is a key part of that transformation. Through Cloud HQ, our strategic approach to distributed work, most employees have the flexibility to work from wherever they’re most productive—enabling us to move fast, stay connected and deliver on our people promise.


Zillow is honored to be recognized among the best workplaces in the U.S. Zillow was named one of FORTUNE 100 Best Companies to Work For® in 2026, and included on TIME’s America’s Best Companies 2026 list, reflecting our commitment to creating an innovative, inclusive, and engaging culture where employees are empowered to grow.


No matter where you sit in the organization, your work will help drive innovation, support our customers, and move the industry—and your career—forward, together.

jobs.description:
Job Description

At GSK, we have bold ambitions for patients, aiming to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade. Our R&D focuses on discovering and delivering vaccines and medicines, combining our understanding of the immune system with cutting-edge technology to transform people’s lives. GSK fosters a culture ambitious for patients, accountable for impact, and committed to doing the right thing, making sure that we focus our efforts on accelerating significant assets that meet patients’ needs and have the highest probability of success. We’re uniting science, technology, and talent to get ahead of disease together.


Job Purpose

US Local Delivery Lead Director provides leadership, oversight and manages the activities of local delivery leads (LDLs) to ensure the delivery of all clinical studies, across all therapy areas (Rx and Vx) to the required quality standards, GSK written standards and ICH GCP. Operates independently and effectively in a highly complex, high volume, strategic market.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Leads a team of LDLs operating in a highly complex environment due to scale (number of subjects/sites per study) and volume (number of studies assigned to country) of studies conducted, providing training, coaching, mentoring, line and performance management.
  • Responsible for effectively managing capacity utilization of LDL resources and contributes to resourcing solutions including multi-country support by LDLs, ensuring alignment of capabilities with study requirements, resource availability and business priorities. Contribute to overall management of clinical research within the LOC via involvement in applicable leadership teams to ensure consistency and utilization of resources and best practice.
  • Accountable for ensuring the completion of all project management deliverables for all studies assigned to the LOC to agreed timelines, budget and quality standards. The LDL manager works with the LDLs to identify and resolve or escalate risks and issues that may impact study delivery.
  • Responsible for identifying and sharing best practices, standardizing across the LOC / region and representing local/regional clinical operations on global and cross functional initiatives. Ability to understand and respond to unique challenges in managing workload due to size and scale of studies.
  • Recruits and develops LDLs. Evaluates capabilities and competencies of internal staff, identifies and coordinates implementation of personal development plans for direct reports.
  • Partners with local and central teams to ensure robust study feasibility with reference to study complexity, clinical facilities and monitoring resource.
  • Establishes and manages key strategic relationships with external vendors to ensure clinical studies are appropriately resourced and executed as necessary.
  • Ensures that critical study timelines related to study activities are accurately forecasted and achieved and that recruitment targets, patient recruitment cycle times, data and audit quality and site related milestones are met. Provides trouble-shooting and problem resolution support for LDLs to ensure productive, efficient study delivery.
  • In collaboration with Clinical Operation Director and Local/Regional Quality, Capability & Risk Manager identifies management monitoring process checks linked with LDL activities that require inclusion in the local quality plan to ensure quality and integrity of clinical studies conducted in the LOC.
  • Assists with audits/inspections of local clinical operations department & study / sites in the country, as required.
  • Continuous development of knowledge in the areas of GCP, internal company guidelines, SOPs, new monitoring technologies and capabilities. Serves as an expert in ICH GCP and GSK written standards for LDLs.
  • Leads or participates in regional/global clinical operations projects (as appropriate).
  • Available and willing to travel as job requires.

Why You?

Basic Qualifications:

  • University degree in Sciences (Medicine, Pharmacy, Biochemistry, Biology or related fields) or equivalent demonstrable professional experience in the area
  • At least 10 years of experience in clinical operations delivery within the pharmaceutical or biotech industry, including leadership of complex, multi‑site clinical studies in the US.
  • At least 5 years of experience leading and developing clinical operations leaders or managers (e.g., LDLs, study managers, CTMs) in a high‑volume, high‑complexity environment.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Demonstrated accountability for study delivery to timelines, quality standards, and regulatory requirements, including risk identification, issue escalation, and problem resolution.
  • Strong working knowledge of ICH‑GCP, GSK written standards, and US regulatory expectations.
  • Experience delivering oncology clinical trials in the US, including studies with large site networks, complex protocols, and competitive enrollment environments.
  • Experience leading delivery across late phase and/or registrational oncology studies is highly valued.
  • Familiarity with oncology specific operational challenges, such as:
    • High protocol complexity and amendment frequency
    • Specialized site types and networks
    • Competitive enrollment and site capacity constraints
  • Experience operating across multiple oncology indications or programs within a portfolio.


Skills

Agile Thinking, Business Acumen, Clinical Data Management, Clinical Development, Clinical Research, Clinical Trials, Communication, Creativity, Decision Making, Pharmaceutical Industry, Project ManagementThe US annual base salary for new hires in this position ranges from $169,500 to $282,500. The US salary ranges take into account a number of factors including work location within the US market, the candidate’s skills, experience, education level and the market rate for the role. In addition, this position offers an annual bonus and eligibility to participate in our share based long term incentive program which is dependent on the level of the role. Available benefits include health care and other insurance benefits (for employee and family), retirement benefits, paid holidays, vacation, and paid caregiver/parental and medical leave. If salary ranges are not displayed in the job posting for a specific country, the relevant compensation will be discussed during the recruitment process.

Please visit GSK US Benefits Summary to learn more about the comprehensive benefits program GSK offers US employees.

Why GSK?

Uniting science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together.

GSK is a global biopharma company with a purpose to unite science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. We aim to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade, as a successful, growing company where people can thrive. We get ahead of disease by preventing and treating it with innovation in specialty medicines and vaccines. We focus on four therapeutic areas: respiratory, immunology and inflammation; oncology; HIV; and infectious diseases – to impact health at scale.

People and patients around the world count on the medicines and vaccines we make, so we’re committed to creating an environment where our people can thrive and focus on what matters most. Our culture of being ambitious for patients, accountable for impact and doing the right thing is the foundation for how, together, we deliver for patients, shareholders and our people.

ABOUT THE COMPANY

Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE: RSG) is a leader in the environmental services industry. We provide customers with the most complete set of products and services, including recycling, waste, special waste, hazardous waste and field services. Our industry-leading commitments to advance circularity and support decarbonization are helping deliver on our vision to partner with customers to create a more sustainable world.


In 2025, Republic’s total company revenue was $16.6 billion, and adjusted EBITDA was $5.3 billion. We serve 13 million customers and operate more than 1,000 locations, including collection and transfer stations, recycling and polymer centers, treatment facilities, and landfills.


Although we operate across North America, the collection, recycling, treatment, or disposal of materials is a local business, and the dynamics and opportunities differ in each market we serve. By combining local operational management with standardized business practices, we drive greater operating efficiencies across the company while maintaining day-to-day operational decisions at the local level, closest to the customer.


Our customers, including small businesses, major corporations and municipalities, want a partner with the expertise and capabilities to effectively manage their multiple recycling and waste streams. They choose Republic Services because we are committed to exceeding their expectations and helping them achieve their sustainability goals. Our 42,000 team members understand that it's not just what we do that matters, but how we do it.


Our company values guide our daily actions:

  • Safe: We protect the livelihoods of our colleagues and communities.
  • Committed to Serve: We go above and beyond to exceed our customers’ expectations.
  • Environmentally Responsible: We take action to improve our environment.
  • Driven: We deliver results in the right way.
  • Human-Centered: We respect the dignity and unique potential of every person.

We are proud of our high employee engagement score of 86. We have an inclusive and diverse culture where every voice counts. In addition, our team positively impacted 5.1 million people in 2024 through the Republic Services Charitable Foundation and local community grants. These projects are designed to meet the specific needs of the communities we serve, with a focus on building sustainable neighborhoods.


STRATEGY

Republic Services’ strategy is designed to generate profitable growth. Through acquisitions and industry advancements, we safely and sustainably manage our customers’ multiple waste streams through a North American footprint of vertically integrated assets.

We focus on three areas of growth to meet the increasing needs of our customers: recycling and waste, environmental solutions and sustainability innovation.

With our integrated approach, strengthening our position in one area advances other areas of our business. For example, as we grow volume in recycling and waste, we collect additional material to bolster our circularity capabilities. And as we expand environmental solutions, we drive additional opportunities to provide these services to our existing recycling and waste customers.


Recycling and Waste

We continue to expand our recycling and waste business footprint throughout North America through organic growth and targeted acquisitions. The 13 million customers we serve and our more than 5 million pick-ups per day provide us with a distinct advantage. We aggregate materials at scale, unlocking new opportunities for advanced recycling. In addition, we are cross-selling new products and services to better meet our customers’ specific needs.


Environmental Solutions

Our comprehensive environmental solutions capabilities help customers safely manage their most technical waste streams. We are expanding both our capabilities and our geographic footprint. We see strong growth opportunities for our offerings, including PFAS remediation, an increasing customer need.

Sustainability Innovation

Republic’s recent innovations to advance circularity and decarbonization demonstrate our unique ability to leverage sustainability as a platform for growth.


The Republic Services Polymer Center is the nation’s first integrated plastics recycling facility. These innovative sites process rigid plastics from our recycling centers, producing recycled materials that promote true bottle-to-bottle circularity. We also formed Blue Polymers, a joint venture with Ravago, to develop facilities that will further process plastic material from our Polymer Centers to help meet the growing demand for sustainable packaging. We are building a network of Polymer Centers and Blue Polymer facilities across North America.


Our customers are increasingly looking for decarbonization solutions, and we are leveraging our network of landfills to meet that need. Republic is committed to harnessing landfill gas, a natural byproduct of decomposing waste, and converting it to energy. Republic has partnered with renewable gas developers to construct Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) plants at our landfills, expanding beyond the 77 projects we currently have to make progress towards our goal to beneficially reuse 50% more biogas by 2030 (2017 baseline year).

jobs.description:
About us

Dyson is a global technology enterprise. We solve the problems others choose to ignore, with surprising new inventions that defy convention and simply work better. We’re growing fast and our ambition is huge – more categories, more locations, and more people.
From its beginnings in cyclonic vacuums, Dyson’s portfolio has grown to include five main areas of technology: Cord-free and corded vacuum cleaners, hand dryers, lighting, environmental control machines (purifying fans, heating and cooling fans and humidifiers) and hair styling tools, which are sold in more than 82 countries across the world. We are on a mission to improve our customer’s lives: whether that be by making the the air they breathe safe and clean, or connecting them to high performing machines, which keep their homes clean.

About the role

Role Overview

The Social Commerce Content Specialist supports the execution and optimization of Dyson Singapore's social commerce content across TikTok Shop and other platforms. The role plans, creates, publishes and optimizes social commerce-native content that supports discovery, engagement, qualified traffic and commerce contribution, while exploring AI-enabled workflows to improve creative speed and production efficiency.

Key Responsibilities

1. Always-On Content Planning

  • Support the development of weekly content plans and publishing schedules based on commercial priorities and campaign requirements.
  • Recommend content themes, product focus areas and campaign support ideas for Dyson's owned social commerce channel.
  • Maintain a strong base bank of planned content while protecting capacity for reactive trends and timely cultural moments.
  • Balance product education, demonstration, problem-solution, creator-led, entertainment and conversion-oriented formats.
  • Plan sufficient content depth to support multiple daily posts during launches and key commercial periods without compromising quality or accuracy.

2. End-to-End Content Creation

  • Spot relevant social trends, behaviors, sounds, formats and hooks; translate them into ideas appropriate for a premium technology brand.
  • Develop concepts, hooks, scripts and shot lists for organic and commerce content, with guidance from the wider team where required.
  • Shoot and edit content using mobile-first workflows and collaborate with internal stakeholders; create platform-native cuts, captions, graphics and sound treatments.
  • Publish content accurately and on time, with correct product naming, claims, links, tags and social commerce Shop product anchors.
  • Explore AI-enabled tools to improve ideation, scripting, editing, localization and content versioning.

3. Content Re-Purposing and Capture

  • Rework suitable global and regional assets into local, social-native edits.
  • Identify and repurpose high-performing material from affiliates, owned livestreams, experts, stylists, launches and events, subject to usage rights.
  • Create content briefs and capture plans for colleagues, creators, and talent, so usable footage is generated efficiently.
  • Maintain an organized content library with clear status, usage rights, product, format, and tags.

4. Trend-Jacking and Reactive Execution

  • Identify reactive opportunities that are relevant to Dyson products, audiences and brand standards.

5. Performance Optimization

  • Track views, watch time, completion, engagement, shares, saves, profile visits, product clicks and video-attributed GMV.
  • Identify winning hooks, formats, products and creators; create follow-up variations and retire approaches that are consistently weak.
  • Provide a concise weekly content readout with insights, next tests and recommended changes, not only a list of posts published.
  • Work with the Social Commerce Lead and Marketing to identify high-performing organic content suitable for paid boosting.

6. Brand and Content Governance

  • Ensure all content meets brand, legal, product-claim, music-rights and platform-compliance requirements.
  • Maintain Dyson's premium positioning while creating content that feels current and native to TikTok.

* Key Performance Indicators

  • Output and Consistency:Agreed owned-channel publishing cadence delivered; planned base content and reactive content produced on time.

  • Speed: Time from trend identification or commercial brief to approved publication.

  • Attention Quality:Average watch time, completion rate, shares, saves and engagement versus benchmarks.

  • Commerce Contribution: Product clicks, click-through rate, video-attributed GMV and qualified content passed for boosting.

  • Learning Velocity​:Number and quality of structured tests, repeatable winning formats and performance-led iterations.

About You

  • 1-2 years' experience in short-form video, social content, creative production or creator-led marketing.
  • Demonstrable social media-native portfolio with strong hooks, pacing, storytelling, product demonstration and editing judgement.
  • Able to concept, script, shoot and edit independently using tools such as CapCut, Premiere Pro or equivalent.
  • Fast and resourceful, with strong trend judgement and discipline to protect premium brand standards.
  • Curious and hands-on with AI content tools, with the ability to test new workflows responsibly and turn successful experiments into repeatable production processes.
  • Strong attention to detail in product claims, captions, tagging, links, file management and publishing accuracy.
  • Able to work with employees, creators, experts and stylists to capture natural, useful content efficiently.

GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

As Manager, SOX PMO - Business Process, you'll lead Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) compliance for assigned business processes as part of GitLab's second line. This is advisory work, not repeatable testing: you'll deeply understand how processes work, evaluate risks as the business changes, and help control owners design and remediate controls that hold up to audit. Judgment matters more than procedure. You'll form well-supported conclusions, align with control owners and Internal Audit, and defend positions to external auditors. GitLab already uses AI extensively, and the next phase brings AI agents into our SOX processes. You'll help teams adopt them with confidence, finding creative ways to enable new ways of working while maintaining compliance. You'll also partner with the information technology (IT) SOX PMO on readiness for new systems and applications. This role reports to the Senior Director, SOX PMO, within the Chief Accounting Officer's organization.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead SOX compliance for assigned business processes as the second-line subject matter expert, advising control owners who own and operate the controls. Deeply understand each process, its systems and data flows, and resolve open questions and assumptions early.
  • Monitor risks from new and changing processes, products, and systems. Help control owners design, strengthen, or right-size controls, and contribute to the annual SOX risk assessment and scoping.
  • Evaluate control deficiencies individually and in aggregate, identify root causes, and prepare well-supported severity assessments. Work with management to develop, implement, and monitor remediation plans.
  • Prepare auditor-ready technical memos on sampling methodology, scoping, and control rationalization, using independent analysis and sound conclusions. Prepare reports and presentations on SOX compliance status for leadership.
  • Lead business walkthroughs and stakeholder meetings, and coordinate with Internal Audit and external auditors throughout the audit. Anticipate questions, support positions with data and judgment, and escalate risks and auditor comments promptly with a recommended path forward.
  • Advise on controls for AI-enabled processes and processes that use AI agents. Find opportunities to automate SOX work using AI tools, and validate their output.
  • Partner with the IT SOX PMO to assess new systems and controls, including application controls and key reports.
  • Develop and maintain accurate process narratives, flowcharts, and risk and control matrices as processes change. Collaborate with Finance, Operations, Legal, Human Resources, Sales, Engineering, and IT leaders to help them design and maintain effective business controls.

What You’ll Bring

  • Hands-on SOX and internal controls experience in control design, remediation, and deficiency evaluation, beyond testing alone. Experience in the software or technology industry is required; SOX PMO, Big Four risk advisory, or assurance experience is a strong plus.
  • A bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field; an active Certified Public Accountant (CPA) credential (strongly preferred) or Certified Internal Auditor (CIA) credential.
  • A strong understanding of SOX requirements and internal control frameworks, such as the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO) framework.
  • Professional judgment and skepticism: verifying facts against source documents, testing the reasonableness of data and conclusions, and recognizing missing information.
  • A track record of independently solving ambiguous, novel problems, from defining an approach through overcoming obstacles and driving resolution. Curiosity to understand how processes actually work and keep learning as the business changes.
  • Clear written and verbal communication, including concise, accurate, auditor-ready memos and actionable recommendations. Confidence partnering with senior stakeholders and external auditors, including working through pushback.
  • A practical, innovative approach to helping the business adopt new technologies, products, and ways of working while maintaining compliance. Experience using AI tools to improve efficiency and validating their output.
  • Experience with usage-based billing or AuditBoard is a plus.

The SOX PMO is part of the Chief Accounting Officer's organization. In this role, you'll advise business control owners and partner with the IT SOX PMO, Internal Audit, and external auditors to keep GitLab compliant as processes, systems, and AI use evolve. GitLab is an all-remote company, with flexibility to work from home or wherever you're most productive. When a member is seeing several providers, it’s easy for a referral, medication question, or follow-up appointment to get lost between offices. As an RN Care Coordinator, you’ll look at the full picture with the member, help determine what needs attention first, and make sure everyone involved in their care has the information they need.

AlediumHR is recruiting for this role on behalf of our client, which supports Medicaid, Medicare Advantage, and Dual Eligible Special Needs Plan (D-SNP) members. You’ll manage your own caseload and work with members by phone and text, including people with complex medical and social needs.

  • Experience communicating with patients or members by phone and text, using motivational interviewing, and documenting in a care management system or electronic health record.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Passionate about SEO, AI, and the future of discovery through LLMs, and comfortable using AI tools like Claude as a core part of your daily work.

jobs.excerpt: En Imagemaker estamos en búsqueda de un líder de Observabilidad.
jobs.description:
En Imagemaker estamos en búsqueda de un líder de Observabilidad. Este rol existe para traducir las exigencias regulatorias y de negocio en una arquitectura de monitoreo end-to-end aprobable por el banco, garantizando que toda la telemetría (logs, trazas y eventos de negocio) se ingeste, correlacione y mida con exactitud antes de salir a producción.

Responsabilidades

  • Diseñar la arquitectura de observabilidad end-to-end (HLD/LLD) aprobada por SRE Central.
  • Definir el catálogo de SLIs, SLOs, error budgets y journeys transaccionales críticos.
  • Especificar la instrumentación de trazas, logs y business events con reglas de privacidad.
  • Desarrollar dashboards ejecutivos y alertas automáticas como código mediante Terraform y Monaco.
  • Auditar la calidad técnica y los pull requests del equipo de observabilidad.
  • Liderar la planificación, el backlog y los riesgos técnicos frente al cliente.
  • Entregar el paquete de promoción a producción.

Requisitos

Imprescindibles (Must-Have)

  • Ingeniería en Dynatrace SaaS (3ª Generación): Dominar el ecosistema nativo en la nube, incluyendo Grail (almacén de datos unificado para logs y eventos), DQL (Dynatrace Query Language o lenguaje de consultas),Notebooks, Dashboards y Business Events (eventos de negocio), descartando perfiles que solo operen versiones clásicas on-premise.
  • Arquitectura de Observabilidad End-to-End: Diseñar soluciones de extremo a extremo bajo la metodología de "diseño antes que construcción", definiendo catálogos de SLIs (Service Level Indicators o indicadores de nivel de servicio), SLOs (Service Level Objectives u objetivos de nivel de servicio), error budgets (presupuestos de error) y mapas de flujos críticos entre sistemas desacoplados.
  • Instrumentación y Telemetría Distribuida: Especificar y validar la captura de trazas distribuidas, logs y métricas mediante Dynatrace OneAgent y estándares de OpenTelemetry, asegurando que las respuestas de los microservicios incluyan los campos del diccionario de datos transaccional.
  • Monitoring as Code (MaC) y Control de Versiones: Desarrollar, versionar y desplegar configuraciones de monitoreo como código (alertas, tableros y objetivos) utilizando Terraform y Monaco (Dynatrace Monitoring as Code) sobre repositorios Git y Bitbucket mediante flujos de aprobación de Pull Requests.
  • Seguridad, Privacidad y Cumplimiento Regulatorio: Implementar reglas estrictas de enmascaramiento y ofuscación de datos sensibles bajo normativas PII (Personally Identifiable Information o información personal identificable) y PCI (Payment Card Industry o industria de tarjetas de pago), garantizando mediciones auditables para entes reguladores.
  • Entornos Cloud Native y Sistemas Operativos: Comprender la arquitectura e ingesta de telemetría sobre clústeres de contenedores en Kubernetes y OpenShift (incluyendo distribuciones Atlas o Anthos), así como entornos base Unix/Linux y consumo de APIs (Application Programming Interfaces o interfaces de programación).

Deseables (Nice-to-Have)

  • Capacidades Avanzadas de IA y Automatización en Dynatrace: Configurar motores de inteligencia artificial causal (Davis AI) para detección automática de anomalías, así como diseñar flujos automatizados (Workflows) y pruebas de monitoreo sintético (Synthetics) para simular transacciones de punta a punta.
  • Certificaciones Oficiales de Dynatrace: Contar con la acreditación Dynatrace Associate (exigida en el pliego formal pero flexibilizada por el cliente frente a experiencia comprobable) o el nivel superior Dynatrace Professional.
  • Experiencia en Banca o Medios de Pago en Tiempo Real: Haber instrumentado ecosistemas financieros de alta criticidad y baja latencia, comprendiendo el ciclo de vida de transferencias interbancarias, cámaras de compensación y reportes regulatorios ante bancos centrales.
  • Inglés Técnico Avanzado: Poseer capacidad de lectura técnica fluida para interpretar documentación oficial de plataformas SaaS y notas de lanzamiento (release notes), complementando el dominio nativo o fluido del español requerido para la operación diaria.
